Thanks for taking the time earlier today — great conversation. This thread captures the items we agreed to triage after the call so the pilot validation run can be scheduled. I’ve pulled out concrete asks so we can keep timing tight.

Key constraints you shared (please correct if I misunderstood):
- Peak concurrent requests: ~1.2k active user sessions at peak (burst window ~3–7 minutes)
- Latency objective: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for short completions (<=256 tokens); tail objectives for streaming partials: first token <= 120ms in the warm path
- Streaming: client requires partial token delivery every ~150ms on average for live UI; total response lengths avg 120–400 tokens
- Expected sustained throughput during burst: equivalent to ~40k tokens/min over the 5-minute peak window

Action items we committed to:
1) Redwood to propose warm-pool sizing and priming strategy that meets the p95 target and first-token streaming timing. (Owner: Karthik + Vivek — deliverable: playbook + priming calc)
2) Onramp to share the real load-profile CSV (attached) and confirm tolerance for queueing vs. hard rejects. (Owner: Eliza)
3) Agree on scale-up SLO (target: 30s to add 100 GPU-backed inference instances to cover burst; TBD) and a fallback plan if the warm pool is insufficient. (Owner: Mina)
4) Schedule validation run with synthetic replay and two-week window for results. (Owner: Mina/Eliza)

Preliminary questions for Karthik/Vivek:
- Do we recommend aggressive KV-cache warmup (full prefix priming) or a lightweight prompt priming approach for fast first-token?
- For the streaming path, is there a recommended per-instance concurrency cap to avoid serialization pauses?

Attachments: onramp_mrp_loadprofile.csv (Samir shared on the call), placeholder: redwood_warmpool_playbook.pdf (draft).

Next steps: Karthik/Vivek — can you put an initial priming + warm-pool sizing proposal in this thread by Monday (2027-10-11)? Eliza/Samir — confirm whether Onramp prefers queueing to 30s or immediate 429 on capacity shortfall. I’ll propose calendar times for the validation run once we have the priming plan.

Mina / Eliza — jumping in with a concise technical recommendation so we can align on the validation test. High-level summary first, details below.

Recommendation (short):
- Warm-pool strategy: hybrid priming — maintain a modest prewarmed pool sized to cover ~40% of short-latency p95 load (recommended starting point: 50 prewarmed instances) and use rapid scale-up + request-level lightweight priming to cover the rest.
- Priming approach: prefix priming for the warm pool (replay of representative prompts) to populate KV cache + a short (2–3 sec) synthetic prompt for newly-provisioned instances to accelerate first-token.
- Streaming config: limit per-instance active streams to ~8 for stable interleaving; higher concurrency increases risk of jitter in first-byte timing.
- Queueing behavior: implement a short soft-queue (20s max) with early fallbacks to a lower-capacity model variant after 10s; if request-age > 20s return 429.

Technical notes and rationale:
1) Why hybrid: full warm coverage for 1.2k concurrent sessions would be expensive; a 50-instance warm pool (GPU-backed) handles the most latency-sensitive fraction and buys time for scale-up. Rapid scale-up using our autoscaler (target ~30s per 100-instance increment in our standard infra) plus lightweight priming reduces cold-start p95 considerably.
2) KV cache priming: for autoregressive models with reused prefixes, replaying representative prefixes reduces token decode work on hot-path. We recommend the attached warmpool playbook (redwood_warmpool_playbook.pdf) with priming templates.
3) Streaming per-instance cap: empirically we see inter-token variance increase when >10 concurrent streaming sessions share a single GPU context and multiplexing buffers; 6–8 is a good practical cap for the client patterns you described.
4) Measurement: Redwood SDK can emit first-token timestamps; we will provide a lightweight telemetry hook you can add for end-to-end first-byte timing.

Next steps (concrete):
- I will upload a warm-pool sizing worksheet showing cost delta and p95 trade-offs by EOD Tue (2027-10-12).
- Schedule a 45m technical test plan review (suggest Tue 10/12 2:00pm PT).
